items.title: Build it from config (AgentCore harness) | Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro 06
items.summary: Level 300. A made-up online shop's help desk is built as an AgentCore harness: you write two files, harness.yaml and system-prompt.md, deploy them with the AgentCore CLI in the Tokyo Region, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runs the loop, the tools from an AgentCore Gateway (deck 04), the memory and the records, while an inline function hands each refund back to the shop's app to wait for the store manager. Real terminal output and figures with the official icons show the stop and the answer, narrowing tools with allowedTools, lifecycle hooks, versions and endpoints that keep production on version 2, export to Strands code, when to choose Runtime instead, and the cleanup; this is deck 06 of the Build it out part of Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro.

items.title: Interventions and plugins (Interrupts, human in the loop, and skills) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 04
items.summary: A deck for Python developers who have built a Strands Agents agent with tools and hooks, on how to put people and rules in the loop. It shows how to ask a person before a risky tool call with HumanInTheLoop and its classifier, how to put Cedar policies in front, and how to stop a call with an interrupt and resume it, also across a client and a server with a session manager. It then shows how plugins bundle hooks and tools, how skills load their instructions only when needed, how intervention handlers return Proceed, Deny, or Guide, and how steering gives feedback in plain words. Every example is real code with its real output, run on Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region with global cross-Region inference, with architecture diagrams and flow charts. The facts come from the official Strands Agents documentation only, and the examples use a help-desk agent with made-up customers and orders, made for this series. As of November 2026 (Strands Agents 1.64, Level 300). This is deck 04 (Go deeper) of the Learn Strands Agents with Kiro series.

items.title: Secure the way in and the way out (AgentCore Identity) | Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro 10
items.summary: This Level 300 deck shows how to check who is calling the help desk agent of a made-up online electronics shop: Amazon Cognito sign-in tokens (JWTs) are checked at the inbound auth of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and AgentCore Gateway, the session ID and memory actorId come from the checked token, and outside credentials are kept in AgentCore Identity so the agent holds no long-lived ones, drawn as architecture and flow diagrams with the official AWS icons. Real terminal output shows calls refused and let through, an API key whose value get does not return, and a stock API closed with IAM, while the API key outbound flow, 3LO and OBO are drawn as flows not run in this deck, as deck 10 (Govern and share) of the series Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro.

items.title: Run it in CI (Kiro CLI headless mode and one readiness check) | Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro 07
items.summary: Level 300. Run the checks you run locally in CI in the same order, keep the heavy ones for the night, and roll every result into one readiness check that says yes only when every check has run and passed. On a small booking app, this deck has headless Kiro CLI review each PR with read-only tools, lets a script decide pass or fail, has Kiro check the running app through a browser MCP, writes the guards for unattended runs into the workflow, and shows the real terminal output of each run. This is deck 07 (Run the loop pillar) of the "Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro" series.

items.title: Contain what the agent can do (Permissions, sandboxes, and .kiroignore) | Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro 06
items.summary: This Level 200 deck shows how to contain what Kiro can do with permissions (deny, ask, allow), the local command sandbox, .kiroignore, and a Pre Tool Use hook, and covers where each rule lives, keeping changes easy to undo, and not locking down too far. On a small booking app, real Kiro CLI screens show a rule refusing to delete the data, the sandbox stopping a connection out, .kiroignore keeping .env unread, and a hook stopping a curl that sends data out, and the deck ends with a first set of settings. This is deck 06 (Contain pillar) of the "Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro" series.
